takeaways.label: Record quarter, guidance raised
takeaways.text: Revenue hit an all-time high of INR696 crores (+22% YoY), and FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was upgraded by 200 bps to 27% ±2% on strong demand and operating leverage.

takeaways.label: Architectural films are the new growth engine
takeaways.text: Once 10% of window film sales, the architectural segment now contributes ~30% (INR400 crores annualized) and is targeted to reach INR1,000 crores, becoming the company’s top priority.

takeaways.label: Margins expanded despite cost headwinds
takeaways.text: EBITDA margin hit 27.2% (up 377 bps YoY) even as raw material and logistics costs created a ~INR37 crores headwind, demonstrating pricing power and mix improvement.

takeaways.label: Two capex cycles will unlock the next leg
takeaways.text: A TPU film line commissions in Q3 FY27, and a new solar control film line (INR191 crores) targets H1 FY28, together adding capacity to reach INR3,500 crores at full utilization.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: TPU line commissioning and ramp, progress on the 50-studio D2C target, and whether architectural growth sustains its 35–40% trajectory into the seasonally weaker Q3.

points.label: Scale and trajectory
points.text: Architectural films have grown from 10% of window film revenue to ~30%, an annualized run rate of roughly INR400 crores. Management expects this share to reach 50% as the business scales toward INR1,000 crores.

points.label: Why it matters
points.text: Management sees architectural as the number-one target segment because of the vast installed base of glass globally, and the film’s value proposition versus glass alone: 20–30% cheaper, 99.9% UV protection (vs. 70% for glass), 20–30% more heat rejection, plus safety benefits.

points.label: Pricing power demonstrated
points.text: Architectural film pricing was repositioned from ~30% of the top global player to 85–120% over 3–4 years by filling product-basket gaps, building dedicated marketing teams in India, the Middle East, and the US, and proving product quality.

points.label: Domestic traction
points.text: The domestic architectural business has grown 3x in top line and ~4–5x in bottom line over three years, driven by a dedicated team and awareness campaigns.

points.label: Capacity aligned to ambition
points.text: The new solar control film line (commercial production H1 FY28) is targeted primarily at the architectural segment, which is expected to grow 35–40%.

quotes.text: Joshi: “We feel the architectural sun control film, architectural segment is going to be like something which we are targeting as number one. ... there is so much of glass around the world, so we are targeting that segment as a top segment for us.”

points.label: Q2 margin performance
points.text: EBITDA margin of 27.2% was the best-ever Q2, expanding 377 bps YoY, even as Q1 (30.3%) benefits from seasonal Sun Control strength. H1 EBITDA margin reached 28.7%.

points.label: Cost headwinds absorbed
points.text: Raw material costs rose ~4% and logistics costs rose INR9 crores in absolute terms, creating a combined INR37 crores headwind in Q2. The company offset this through realization, favorable product mix, and operating leverage.

points.label: Product-level margin structure
points.text: Sun Control top products earn 40–45% EBITDA, medium products 30–35%, and PPF earns 20–25%. The growing share of high-margin architectural Sun Control films supports blended margin expansion.

points.label: Crude oil resilience
points.text: At \$100–\$110 crude, the company delivered these numbers. Management notes that 75% of the business has low crude correlation (10–12% for Sun Control, 5–7% for PPF) because value addition from adhesives, nanoparticles, coatings, and liners dilutes the base-film link.

points.label: Long-term crude tailwind
points.text: Management’s view is that crude realistically may not be even \$50 to \$60 in 3–5 years as EVs and alternative fuels reduce demand, which would significantly benefit margins across packaging, transportation, dyes, and chemicals.

quotes.text: Joshi: “My assessment was that if we are able to do at \$100 and \$110 these kind of numbers, definitely we are poised for much bigger and better growth for future.”

sections.title: Capacity Expansion: Two Lines, One Timeline

points.label: TPU film line
points.text: Commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27. The line will supply 75% of output internally to the PPF business (reducing manufacturing cost and adding 150–200 bps of consolidated margin) and 25% as external merchant sales.

points.label: Solar control film line
points.text: The INR191 crores expansion is progressing with a focus on robotics and automation. Commercial production is expected in H1 FY28, roughly by June 2027, with efforts to pull the timeline forward. The line adds ~12 crore sq ft of fungible capacity, primarily for architectural films.

points.label: Revenue potential at full utilization
points.text: With both new lines, the company can reach up to INR3,500 crores at full utilization, though the exact number depends on product mix. The new Sun Control line alone can contribute roughly INR450–500 crores, and PPF can add ~INR250 crores from current levels.

points.label: Fungibility as a safety valve
points.text: If PPF demand rises faster than expected, some Sun Control plant capacity can be used as fungible capacity to sustain growth in both segments.

points.label: Utilization trajectory
points.text: Sun Control utilization was 75% in Q2, PPF at 73%. Both are expected to approach 100% by Q1 FY28. PPF is expected to reach 90–95% within the next six months.

points.label: Future capex signaled
points.text: Management confirmed the company is working toward more investment in the next three years for architectural film and TPU film businesses, but declined to provide specifics until board approval.

quotes.text: Joshi: “We will definitely aim in next 3 years more investment, but as of now, I can't tell unless it is approved by the board... company is working towards it because of the growth momentum which we are seeing now in architectural film business and the TPU film business.”

points.label: Strategic MOU
points.text: The partnership with Lubrizol (the number-one global supplier of Aliphatic TPU resins) covers development of advanced TPU-based film solutions in India. Lubrizol supplies resin, provides technology for specific applications, and introduces Garware to OEMs. Garware commits to buying a certain volume of resin.

points.label: Fifth vertical
points.text: TPU-based product lines represent a new fifth vertical for the company, alongside industrial, automotive Sun Control, PPF, and architectural Sun Control. Products include front windshield films for buses and trucks, air bladders for high-end cars, and LED applications.

points.label: External sales target
points.text: The company expects INR75–100 crores in external TPU sales in FY28 (not the current year), with an expected EBITDA margin of ~35%.

points.label: Backward integration payoff
points.text: 75% of TPU output going to internal PPF production will reduce manufacturing cost, contributing 150–200 bps of margin expansion at the consolidated level.

points.label: SEMA show response
points.text: Management noted very good response from US participants on the Lubrizol partnership at the SEMA show.

points.label: Home Solutions studios
points.text: The network expanded from 9 in Q1 to 14 in Q2, with plans to add another 12 in Q3 (including Delhi NCR and Mumbai). The longer-term target is 50 studios by December 2027.

points.label: Revenue trajectory
points.text: D2C is a three-year value-creation play, not a one-year sprint. Management targets INR50 crores next year, then INR100 crores, then INR200 crores.

points.label: Strategic intent
points.text: The D2C channel is designed to create value with each home buyer or home owner rather than chase volume at lower prices. Studio locations are carefully selected for grip on home solutions and home furnishing.

points.label: Digital footprint
points.text: Instagram grew 25% YoY, Facebook 10% YoY, global LinkedIn 400%, website traffic reached 1.1 lakh visitors per month, and the annualized digital footprint hit 18 crores.

points.label: Global distribution
points.text: The company added 4 global distributors and opened 2 additional global application studios in the US during Q2, taking the international network to 14 studios.

quotes.text: Joshi: “For us, volume raising is never a problem. We can sell any product in big quantities at lower prices. But what we want here, we want to create value with each home buyer or home owner who wants to buy this product.”

points.label: Export/domestic ratio
points.text: 80/20 in Q2, expected to be broadly maintained even at a INR3,000–3,500 crores run rate, with both exports and domestic growing at 25–30% CAGR.

points.label: Value-added concentration
points.text: 86% of H1 revenue came from value-added products, underscoring the growing contribution of niche, differentiated, higher-value products.

items.title: Group revenue and margin guide
items.text: Management guides to ₹3,500 crore revenue at full utilization of the TPU and new sun control lines (vs ₹2,384 crore now), with consolidated EBITDA margin of 27% plus 1.5-2% from TPU over FY28-FY31. That frames roughly ₹1,100 crore of revenue headroom already funded from internal accruals.

items.title: New sun control film line
items.text: The board approved (6 May 2026) the company's largest-ever capex, a ₹191 crore, 1,200 LSF lamination line at Waluj - a ~30% capacity addition on the existing 4,200 LSF - with commercial production expected around June 2027. It is expected to add ₹450-500 crore of revenue, skewed to the higher-margin architectural segment.

items.title: TPU line and Lubrizol partnership
items.text: India's first aliphatic TPU extrusion line (₹118 crore, 360 LSF) is on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning, backed by a 23 Sep 2026 MoU with Lubrizol to localize ESTANE® TPU in India and jointly promote Garware to US OEMs. The captive 75% drives the guided 150-200 bps margin lift in FY28, and merchant sales should add ₹75-100 crore at ~35% EBITDA margin.

items.title: Architectural films scale-up
items.text: Architectural films have reached a ~₹400 crore annualized run rate (~30% of sun control sales) after tripling revenue in three years, with prices raised to 85-120% of global peers and a 35-40% growth target. Management sees a ₹1,000 crore opportunity, with segment EBITDA margins guided at 25% ±2%.

items.title: PPF ramp-up to 600 LSF
items.text: The second PPF line, commissioned September 2025, ran at 73% utilization in Q2 FY27 versus ~90% expected within six months, with fungible sun control capacity available for first-pass PPF. Management estimates PPF can add around ₹250 crore of revenue from current levels as the line fills.

items.title: MENA expansion and UAE subsidiary
items.text: Middle East/North Africa sales, roughly $15 million and targeted at $20-22 million this year, doubled in a year, and the wholly owned Dubai trading subsidiary (incorporated April 2026) should show full business impact in H2 FY27. Agreements with top regional real estate and architectural companies make MENA the biggest growth driver per management.

items.title: Anti-dumping duty on Chinese PPF
items.text: The DGTR has recommended anti-dumping duty on Chinese TPU-based PPF imports; as of Q2 FY27 the Commerce Ministry had approved it, but the Finance Ministry did not apply it, and the company is taking steps to make that happen. With India PPF penetration at ~3% of cars sold versus ~20% in the US and China, a level playing field supports both market growth and domestic margins.

items.title: Application studio network
items.text: The India PPF studio network crossed 250 stores, and international studios reached 14 (11 USA, 3 Middle East) after Q2 FY27 additions, targeting >300 India + US & MENA in FY27. D2C channels earn 25-30% higher margins than distributor sales, so the shift toward 50% of volumes via studios directly lifts PPF profitability.
